questions.question: Arthur feels that when starting a business, mistakes should be

analyses.content: Arthur认为做生意时犯错是在所难免的，你必须把它们看作是一种积极的经历，从而保证以后不再犯同样的错，这也就是把犯错视为学习的机会。
录音中虽然出现了“无法承担错误（can't afford to make mistakes）”和“无法预测（predict）”，但前者是他要反驳的别人观点，后者是说错误防不胜防，你如果只听这几个单词很容易被干扰选错B或C。

Well, one thing I've heard people say is that when you're starting up a business, you can't afford to make mistakes. Well, I believe in the old saying, "A person who never made a mistake, never made anything." Ha. You can't really predict when you'll make mistakes, and you have to look at them as a positive experience, and one that means you won't make the same mistake again.

questions.question: Recent American studies found that confidence will

analyses.content: 录音提到一个人可能会“自信过头（too much confidence）”且单靠自信不足以保证成功，这就说明自信有时反而会降低人们成功的机会。
你如果听到“买书（buying...books）”和“保证成功（guarantee success）”就去选B或C，说明你漏听了前面的否定词“isn't enough”和后面的负面评价“wasting their time（浪费时间）”。

But according to recent American business school studies, believing in yourself isn't enough by itself to guarantee success. Confidence can be a good thing, but a person can have too much confidence. And people who try to learn to be confident by buying those how to succeed books are just wasting their time.

questions.question: The American studies recommended that new entrepreneurs

analyses.content: 录音明确建议你要“永远把目标记在心里（keep your goals in mind）并永不放弃”，这完美对应了选项中的“保持对目标的专注”。
你可能听到录音里的“listen to... people around you”或者“goes wrong”，但录音实际表达的是“不要听（don't listen to）”旁人的风言风语，遇到困难时也没有建议去寻找专业帮助，切忌断章取义选A或B。

The advice given in these American studies was that being a successful entrepreneur comes down to having the right attitude. It's no good getting depressed every time something goes wrong. Always keep your goals in mind and never give up, and don't listen to all the people around you who say, "Oh, this will never work."

questions.question: What does Arthur say about his own experience of marketing?

analyses.content: Arthur说他意识到自己不懂如何推销，所以找了一个更懂行的人来帮他打理营销方面的事情，也就是雇佣了一位专家。
你可能听到他一开始说“什么都想自己做（tried to do it all myself）”或懂水管的“everything”而误选A，但他马上用“but”转折说明自己不懂营销，最终找了别人代劳。

One thing I've learned in business is that you don't have to be an expert in everything, like marketing, for example. When I started my business, I tried to do it all myself, but I soon realized that although I knew everything there was to know about plumbing, I didn't have much idea about how to sell my ideas. So I got someone who knew more about this to take care of the marketing side of things for me.

questions.question: What does Arthur think is an important quality shared by good leaders?

analyses.content: 录音指出领导者必须是让员工“仰望、钦佩（look up to）”的人，这直接等同于赢得了员工的尊重。
你可能因为听到了“control people”或“make their companies successful”而想选A或B，但在录音中，后者被批评为容易导致“冷酷无情（ruthless）”的管理方式，并不是他认可的优秀品质。

And as for leadership, well, you've got to be someone your workers look up to because you've been seen to make the right decisions. You have to be able to control people but listen to them at the same time. Some people are driven to make their companies successful, but that too often leads to a ruthless approach.

questions.question: What does Arthur say about taking risks?

analyses.content: Arthur个人认为在面对短期风险时，最好还是“小心行事（tread carefully）”，这就表明他在建议大家保持谨慎。
如果你只抓听到了“short-term”就反向推测选B（长期目光），或者听到“increase profits”就选C，说明你没有听到他说被利润冲昏头脑容易“失去的比得到的还多（losing more than you gain）”这一核心警告。

Then there's the question of taking risks, even calculated ones. I personally feel it's actually better to tread carefully when it comes to taking short-term risks. You need a degree of vision, certainly, but it's easy to get carried away by your desire to increase profits. And if things go wrong, you can end up losing more than you gain.

questions.question: Which TWO things does Arthur say people should focus on when developing their business idea?

analyses.content: 录音建议你反问自己能不能“比现有公司更好地满足人们的需求（cater for people's needs better than existing companies）”，这等同于为顾客提供比竞争对手更好的交易或产品。
录音明确提到“不需要担心是否原创（don't need to worry about whether it's original）”，你如果没听到否定词就极易错选A；另外要注意“existing companies”就是选项中“competitors”的同义替换。

So if you have a great idea for a business, what should you do next? Well, the first thing to ask yourself is whether there's a need for your product or service. Can you cater for people's needs better than existing companies? You don't need to worry about whether it's original or not, because there isn't always enough of a demand for completely new ideas.

questions.question: Which TWO things does Arthur say people should focus on when developing their business idea?

analyses.content: 录音强调你需要问自己是否足够在乎这个想法，甚至愿意“奉献接下来十年的生命（dedicate the next ten years of my life to it）”，这就要求你对商业理念有极强的承诺和投入。
你可能会听到录音里出现“color”或“cost”就想选D（关注细节）或E（制定价格），但这些词前面跟着大大的否定词“not”，是在教你不要过早去纠结这些问题。

And the second thing to ask yourself is not what color should the packet be or how much should it cost, but do I care enough about this idea to dedicate the next ten years of my life to it? Because realistically, that's how long it will take.

questions.question: Which TWO things does Arthur say helped him get his business started?

analyses.content: Arthur回忆起步时，提到妻子有一份好工作可以支付家庭的日常开销（pay the household bills），这是帮他渡过难关的最直接的家庭支持。
如果你没有将“妻子（wife）”和“支付家庭开销（household bills）”具象化为家庭支持，很容易漏选；同时，录音明确指出银行“不提供支持（weren't being...supportive）”，直接排除了选项B。

Tell us how you got started, Arthur. How do you explain your early success? Well, I started my business just as the economy was going into a recession, which wasn't the best time, and I was lucky to survive, especially as the banks weren't being particularly supportive to small businesses at that time. Mm. If I'd listened to the business advice I was given back then, I'd never have got started. My strengths were that I knew I could provide a better service than my competitors, who really hadn't spotted the opportunities that were out there, and that my wife had a good job and was able to pay the household bills while I was getting the company on its feet. The first couple of years were very tough, but I knew I would make it eventually.

questions.question: Which TWO things does Arthur say helped him get his business started?

analyses.content: 他指出自己的成功优势在于能比对手提供更好的服务，并抓住了别人没看到的市场机会（spotted the opportunities），这就是一种非常有效的商业方法。
